content.title: Evaluating Long-term Performance on Underpriced IPOs: An Event-time Study on Listings in the Nordic Markets
content.text: AbstractThis thesis investigates the long-term performance of 209 Nordic initial public offerings (IPOs) from 2003 to 2021, revealing no significant differences in the three-year abnormal returns between initially underpriced and overpriced IPOs. The study employs the event-time methodology, evaluating cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) and buy-and-hold abnormal returns (BHAR) against a triple-benchmark group in both equally-weighted and value-weighted calculations. Value-weights are determined using a capped version of the float-adjusted market capitalization. Moreover, a bootstrapping methodology was applied to the BHAR calculations to correct for the inherent positive skewness in stock returns. Amid existing literature documenting mixed long-term IPO performance, this research finds that Nordic IPOs generally outperform the broader market, however no significant differences emerges among the long-term performance of initially underpriced and overpriced IPOs. However, cross-country analyses show differing results, with initially underpriced IPOs outperforming overpriced ones in Norway, while the opposite trend is observed in Denmark. In order to identify determinants of long-term IPO performance, OLS regressions were conducted, incorporating relevant explanatory variables. Consistent with previous literature, the results indicate relatively strong statistical significance that the firm's size positively influence long-term performance. Similarly, there is also a positive relationship between firm age and long-term performance, however at overall weak to no statistical significance. Moreover, compared to manufacturing companies, firms in the Financial & Insurance sectors have a positive relationship with long-term performance, with a high degree of statistical significance. Conversely, the study finds overall strong statistical significance of firms in Information & Communication, Construction and Trade & Transport, to have a negative relationship with long-term performance. Additionally, IPOs listed in Denmark, compared to those in Norway, also positively affect long-term performance, also with high degree of statistical significance.
